title: Are You Learning Biological Signal or Shortcuts? Auditing and Mitigating Bias in Protein-Protein Interaction Datasets
abstract: arXiv:2609.10193v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Protein-protein interaction (PPI) databases do not faithfully reflect biological realities. Instead, they are influenced by study and technical biases that distort certain protein and interaction attributes. Machine learning models can exploit these as learning shortcuts if the negative dataset is not constructed with care. So far, the shortcuts introduced during PPI dataset construction have only been examined in isolation. Here, we systematically characterize both reported and, to our knowledge, previously unreported biases in PPI datasets that lead machine learning models to learn shortcuts instead of biological signal. We analyze HIPPIE, IntAct, and STRING, dedicated PPI databases, as well as two datasets derived from 3D-structural information in the Protein Data Bank (PDB). translated_title: 你在学习生物信号还是捷径？蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用数据集中的偏差审计与缓解
translated_abstract: 蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）数据库并不能忠实反映生物学现实。相反，它们受到研究和实验偏差的影响，这些偏差扭曲了某些蛋白质和相互作用的属性。如果负样本数据集构建不当，机器学习模型可能会将这些偏差当作学习捷径加以利用。迄今为止，PPI数据集构建过程中引入的捷径仅被孤立地研究过。本文中，我们系统地表征了PPI数据集中已报道的以及（据我们所知）此前未被报道的偏差，这些偏差会导致机器学习模型学习捷径而非生物信号。我们分析了HIPPIE、IntAct和STRING这三个专门的PPI数据库，以及两个源自蛋白质数据库（PDB）中3D结构信息的数据集。我们证明了随机数据划分会引入强烈的拓扑捷径。当移除训练集与测试集之间的蛋白质重叠后，所产生的数据集仍然……
tldr: 本文系统审计了蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用数据集中已报道和未报道的多种偏差（包括随机数据划分引入的拓扑捷径），这些偏差会使机器学习模型学到捷径而非真正的生物信号，并提出相应的缓解方法。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically audits both reported and previously unreported biases in protein-protein interaction datasets—showing that random data splitting introduces strong topological shortcuts—and proposes mitigation strategies so machine learning models learn biological signal rather than shortcuts.
